You are reviewing GitHub PR #68 in the repo at /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa. The branch `feature/SFCC-194_pdp-was-now-price` is ALREADY CHECKED OUT. Do NOT modify, stage, commit, or check out anything — read-only review.

YOUR SCOPE: **styling, CSS structure, and design tokens ONLY.** Another agent covers conventions; another covers logic. Stay in your lane.

Primary file under review:
- overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductPrice/zimmProductPrice.css.ts
Also check styling aspects of:
- overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductPrice/index.tsx
- overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductContent/index.tsx
- overrides/app/pages/product-detail/partials/staticProductHeader.tsx

Read these rule files FIRST and treat them as the standard:
- .claude/rules/css.md
- .claude/rules/overrideStyling.md  (the whole file — especially "The hierarchy", "Units", "Component-local tokens", "One canonical styling surface per component type", "Co-locating a component's theme file")
- .claude/rules/protectedFiles.md and .claude/rules/frozenFiles.md (to determine the TIER of every file touched, and whether any Tier 1/Tier 2 gate applies)

THE MOST IMPORTANT TASK — **verify every design token actually exists.** Do not assume. For each `var(--zimm-*)` reference and each bare token key (e.g. `textStyle: 'price'`) in the changed styling code, prove it resolves:
- `--zimm-*` CSS custom properties are defined in `overrides/app/theme/foundation/zimmTokens.ts`. Grep it. A `var(--zimm-...)` that is not defined there resolves to nothing and the property is silently dropped — that is a real visual bug, not a nit.
- `textStyle` values are registered in `overrides/app/theme/foundation/typography.ts`. Confirm the exact key used exists.
- Pay very close attention to the numeric `--zimm-scale-NNN` aliases. overrideStyling.md states only a specific set of numeric aliases exist (025, 700, 1100, 1200, 1300, 3500, 4500) alongside the *named* scale (2xs, xs, s, m, l, xl, 2xl, 3xl...). Verify against zimmTokens.ts whether the specific alias used in this PR is real.
- Verify the colour vars used (`--zimm-color-text-secondary`, `--zimm-color-status-success`, `--zimm-color-text-default`) exist and check what hex each resolves to.

ALSO CHECK:
1. **Recipe registration** — a co-located `<name>.css.ts` must still be registered in `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` under the exact string key the component passes to `useMultiStyleConfig`. Verify the key matches EXACTLY (the component uses a const — check its value).
2. **Multi-part recipe correctness** — the recipe declares `parts: [...]`. Verify that a multi-part recipe consumed via `useMultiStyleConfig` with this shape actually works in this Chakra version: check how OTHER multi-part recipes in this repo are authored (e.g. `overrides/app/components/footer/footer.css.ts`, `footer/bottomBar/bottomBar.css.ts`, any `ui-kits` recipe) and whether they use the same structure. Report any structural mismatch — e.g. `baseStyle` defining only SOME parts while variants define others, or a `variants.default: {}` empty object where siblings define all parts.
3. **The bare-token-key guard** — `overrides/app/theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts` mechanically fails the build on a bare Chakra token key used on a registered scale. Read that test, understand exactly what it walks and what it flags, then determine whether this PR's recipe passes or trips it. Note that `textStyle` is a documented exception.
4. **Raw values** — any raw hex/px/rem/em literal in a component or recipe file. Check whether `npm run audit:tokens` would flag it and whether an acknowledged-exception comment (`provisional`/`pending`/`placeholder`/`audit-allow`) is present.
5. **Namespacing** — recipeGuards.test.ts has a namespacing guard (recipes must not accidentally inherit base SFCC config). Check the recipe's export name and registration key against that guard.
6. **Styling-layer boundary** — `var(--zimm-*)` belongs in the theme recipe, NOT in component JSX/`sx`/style props. Check whether any raw token or hardcoded style leaked into the `.tsx` files (e.g. `opacity={0}`, inline props). Judge whether each such prop is a legitimate Chakra prop or a styling concern that belongs in the recipe.
7. **Accessibility of the colour choices** — the recipe comment claims specific contrast ratios (e.g. "grey[600] #666666, 5.74:1 on white — WCAG AA" and "text.muted grey[300] #969696, 2.95:1"). VERIFY these: look up the actual hex values in `overrides/app/theme/foundation/colour.ts`, confirm the var maps to the hex claimed, and recompute the contrast ratio against the actual background. Report if any claimed number is wrong. Target is WCAG 2.2 AA (4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text ≥18.66px bold or ≥24px) — check the actual rendered font size from the `textStyle` to pick the right threshold.

METHOD — closed loop:
- Every finding must be verified by opening the real file. Report the exact grep/file evidence inline.
- Mark each finding CONFIRMED (verified in-file) or PLAUSIBLE.
- If you claim a token is missing, show the grep you ran that found nothing, and also try plausible alternate spellings before concluding.

OUTPUT: Start with a short table: every token/textStyle reference in the PR → EXISTS / MISSING → resolved value. Then a ranked finding list: `file:line` — severity (Blocker / Major / Minor / Nit) — defect — rule violated — CONFIRMED/PLAUSIBLE. Then a 3-line verdict on styling alignment. No preamble.

# Styling an Override Component

How to style a component under `overrides/app/components/` or `overrides/app/theme/`.
Cross-references [overrides.md](./overrides.md) (module-replacement correctness — a
different concern: that file is about not breaking SFCC's own imports, this one is
about what values to reach for once the component compiles). Day-to-day CSS/token
rules live in [css.md](./css.md); this file is the practical "what do I actually type"
companion.

---

## The hierarchy — reach for these in order

1. **`textStyle` prop** for anything textual. `textStyle="body2"`, never a raw `fontSize`.
   All 22 Handover text styles are registered in `theme/foundation/typography.ts`.
2. **Raw `var(--zimm-*)` CSS custom properties** for colour and spacing — `color="var(--zimm-color-text-default)"`,
   `bg="var(--zimm-color-bg-02)"`, `gap="var(--zimm-scale-m)"`. **Never** a bare Chakra/theme
   token string (`color="text.default"`, `gap="m"`) — even though `theme.colors`/`theme.space`
   ARE registered from the same Zimmermann foundations (see `theme/index.ts`'s own comment on
   which scales are and aren't registered) and a bare key resolves to the identical value. This
   is a house-style requirement, not a correctness one: a `var(--zimm-*)` reference is
   unambiguous at every call site, where a bare key forces a PR reviewer to check
   `theme/index.ts`'s registered-scale list to know whether it happens to be correct. Mechanically
   enforced across every recipe file by `theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts`'s "no
   override-component style uses a bare token key on a registered scale" test — it walks the
   registered recipe map only, so it cannot see the same mistake made as a JSX/`sx` prop (see
   that test's SCOPE note); apply the same discipline there by hand.
3. **A component's own theme config** — either centralized (`theme/components/<name>.ts`)
   or, per the co-location pattern below, beside the component as `<name>.css.ts` — for
   anything that needs to vary by variant/size/state and isn't already a Chakra prop — see
   "Component-local tokens" and "Co-locating a component's theme file" below. For an
   interactive component with existing Chakra support (buttons, inputs, etc.), this theme
   config is the single source of truth — see "One canonical styling surface per component
   type" below.
4. **`sx` prop** for a one-off Chakra-prop-system gap, per [css.md](./css.md).
5. **Scoped `.scss`** only when `sx` genuinely can't express it (complex pseudo-selectors,
   keyframes) — same file, same rules as [css.md](./css.md) already documents.

**Never**: a raw hex/px/rem/em literal in a component file — reach for the token
instead. The one standing exception is `zimmButton.css.ts`'s provisional height/padding
constants (`BTN_HEIGHT_LG`/`BTN_HEIGHT_SM`/`BTN_PADDING_Y`), pending UI-designer
sign-off — see Units below. Run `npm run audit:tokens` (`node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs`)
before opening a PR that touches `overrides/app/components/**` or
`overrides/app/theme/components/**` — it greps for exactly this, scoped to those two paths
(`.ts`/`.tsx`/`.scss`, excluding `*.test.ts(x)` and `*.stories.tsx`). A match is downgraded
from a failure to an acknowledged exception when the surrounding comment block already
contains `provisional`, `pending`, `placeholder`, or an explicit `audit-allow: <reason>` —
the exact vocabulary this codebase already uses for its documented raw-value exceptions, so
existing well-commented code doesn't need a second, separately-maintained allow-list. Built
2026-08-23 — it is not wired into CI yet, deliberately: someone still needs to own triaging a
full run's worth of pre-existing findings first (a first run against this repo surfaced 14
genuine pre-existing violations, none touched by that session, all outside its scope to fix).
Note this is a *different, broader* check than `recipeGuards.test.ts`'s bare-token-key guard
mentioned above: that one exists and runs today (`npm run test`), but only catches a bare
Chakra key standing in for a zimm var — it says nothing about a raw hex/px/rem/em literal,
which is what `audit:tokens` is for.

## Units

- **`rem`** for anything that should scale with the user's root font-size / browser zoom
  (WCAG 1.4.4): type (`fontSize`, `lineHeight`, `letterSpacing`) and spacing
  (`spacing.ts`'s named scale). Letter-spacing values that were specified as sub-pixel px
  in the source don't round to clean rem numbers, so those keep a trailing `// -0.12px`
  comment for traceability.
- **`px`** for hairline geometry that should _not_ scale: border widths, focus-ring
  offsets, and (for now) the provisional button-height constants in `zimmButton.css.ts` that are
  still pending UI-designer sign-off against Handover.
- **`em`** only for breakpoints (`gridSystem.ts` — deliberate, so `.zimm-grid`'s media
  queries shift with zoom the same way Chakra's responsive props do) and other
  genuinely context-relative cases. Not a general-purpose unit.

## The alias tier is a reference, not a second copy

`theme/foundation/colour.ts`'s primitive tier (`grey`, `ivory`, ...) is defined first as
plain `const`s, and the semantic/alias tier below it (`text`, `background`, `border`,
...) reads from those consts (`text.default: grey[900]`) instead of retyping the hex
value. Do the same for any new primitive/alias pair you add — two values can't disagree
if only one of them is ever typed.

`zimmTokens.ts` (the `--zimm-*` CSS-var registry for `globalStyles.ts`'s `.zimm-*`
classes) is fully derived the same way — it imports `colors`/`spacing`/`fontSizes`/
`lineHeights`/`letterSpacings`/`fontWeights`/`iconSizes`/`actionSizes`/`motion`/`grid`
from their owning files rather than retyping values. The only literals left are the 7
numeric `--zimm-scale-NNN` aliases with no named-scale equivalent (`025`, `700`, `1100`,
`1200`, `1300`, `3500`, `4500`) — not duplicates, just Handover values with nothing to
derive them from. `theme/index.test.tsx`'s collision-guard tests still exist as a
regression net; treat a failure there as a real drift signal, not test noise.

## One canonical styling surface per component type

Only one place should define how a given interactive component looks: its theme config —
either centralized as `theme/components/<name>.ts` or, per the co-location pattern below,
beside the component as `<name>.css.ts` — consumed via Chakra's component (`<Button>`,
`<Link>` variant, etc.). Don't also give it a `.zimm-*` global class in
`globalStyles.ts` — a static CSS class can't express `_hover`/`_active`/`_disabled`/
`_focusVisible` states the way a Chakra theme config can, so a class "mirror" is
structurally incomplete from the start, and nothing stops its values from disagreeing
with the real theme config over time. `zimmButton.css.ts` (co-located at `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmButton/`) is the single source of truth for
button styling; `globalStyles.ts` has no `.zimm-btn-*` classes — use Chakra's `<Button>`
for any button, not a class.

`.zimm-*` classes remain the right tool for genuinely static, non-interactive,
massively-reused treatments (typography, the responsive grid, form-field layout) where
there's no interactive state to lose.

## Importing an already-overridden component from a new component

If component A (e.g. `productDetailOptions`) uses component B, and B already has an
override (e.g. `swatch-group`), **import B via a relative path
(`'../swatch-group'`), not the SFCC base path
(`'@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/swatch-group'`)** — even though the
base path is exactly what [overrides.md](./overrides.md) requires _inside_ an override
that's itself shadowing an SFCC module (see `product-tile/index.tsx`'s `DisplayPrice`
import, which is correct for that file).

The reason the two cases differ: the resolver that redirects
`@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` imports to `overrides/` (`ccExtensibility` in
`package.json`, read by a webpack plugin) only runs in the **real app build** — dev
server and production. `.storybook/main.js` aliases that package straight to
`node_modules` and `vitest.config.ts` doesn't touch it at all, so neither loads the
resolver. A base-path import of an already-overridden component will build and run
correctly in the shipped app, but silently render/test the **unstyled base SFCC
version** in Storybook and Vitest — the story or test looks like it's exercising your
override and isn't.

**Known instance of this, not yet fixed:** `product-tile/index.tsx`'s `DisplayPrice`
import uses the base path. Currently dormant only because its Storybook story exercises
the `CardBaseline` named export (which takes `price` as a pre-rendered node and never
calls `DisplayPrice`), not the default `ProductTile` bridge that actually renders it —
worth fixing before anything writes a story/test against the default export.

An override component's own base-path imports (of modules it is _not_ also
overriding) are unaffected by this — `RecommendedProducts`, `Seo`, `QuantityPicker`
etc. have no local override to miss, so the base path is simply correct for them.

## Component-local tokens

When a component needs a spacing/sizing value that already has a `spacing.ts` /
`iconSizes` / etc. entry, reference that entry **as a `var(--zimm-*)` custom property**
— `marginBottom: 'var(--zimm-scale-xs)'`, not `marginBottom: 2`, not
`marginBottom: '0.5rem'`, and **not** the bare key `marginBottom: 'xs'`. The bare-key
form resolved correctly against the registered `theme.space` and was what this section
used to recommend, but hierarchy point 2 above now forbids it and
`theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts`'s bare-token guard **fails the build on it** —
so following the old advice inside a registered recipe breaks `npm run test`.

See `overrides/app/components/footer/footer.css.ts` and
`.../footer/bottomBar/bottomBar.css.ts` for the pattern in a real recipe. The reason is
traceability, not parity with the base theme: a `var(--zimm-*)` reference names the
Figma token it came from, where a raw `2` or `'0.5rem'` names nothing. (Note these
recipes are deliberately namespaced `ZimmFooter*` so they do **not** inherit the base
SFCC `Footer` config — their values come from Figma, not from re-expressing base
numerics. See `recipeGuards.test.ts`'s namespacing guard.)

**Responsive steps are explicit media queries, not Chakra's array shorthand.** A
co-located recipe keys them off `BP` in `theme/components/footerShared.ts`, in the form:

```ts
[`@media (min-width: ${BP.tablet})`]: { gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-3xl)' },
```

The array shorthand (`['2xs', '2xs', 'xs', 'xs']`) is what this section used to
recommend, and it would put a bare token key back at every step — the guard walks
responsive arrays and attributes each element to the same prop, so all four fail.
`footer.css.ts`'s `contentRow` and `linksInner` parts are the reference.

When a component needs a dimension with **no existing foundation entry** (and you don't
have a confirmed Figma value for it), leave it inherited from the base SFCC theme rather
than inventing a number — don't guess at design values. Follow the precedent already in
`header.ts`/`zimmButton.css.ts`: if you do have to ship a placeholder value pending designer
sign-off, say so in a comment next to it, the same way those files already do.

## The SFCC bridge pattern (shared components only)

If the component is used internally by SFCC's own base components (check with `grep -r
"from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/<name>'"
node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/`), its **default export must stay a
faithful, undecorated port** — full original prop surface, same `forwardRef` behaviour,
matching what [overrides.md](./overrides.md) already requires for correctness. Put

import type { SystemStyleObject } from '@chakra-ui/react';

/**
 * Recipe for the PDP `Content` group — the DS's own 218 x 82 frame holding name, price and
 * description. Not an invented grouping.
 *
 * The 20px rhythm is a flex `gap`, not a margin on each child. Two reasons:
 *
 *  - It collapses correctly when an optional field is absent. `ZimmProductDescription` returns
 *    `null` when the product has no description, so there is no second gap to suppress. A
 *    per-child `marginBottom` would need the parent to know which children rendered, and would
 *    leave a trailing gap when the last one did not.
 *  - It cannot be out-specified by a child. An adjacent-sibling rule (`& > * + *`) was tried

{"body":"## Summary

- Introduces `ZimmProductPrice` atom (PRC-09) that renders a single formatted price in the default state and a two-span Was/Now treatment when `originalPrice` is supplied. Styling lives in a co-located `zimmProductPrice.css.ts` recipe with `default` and `sale` multi-part variants; the `sale` variant switches the container to a flex row, mutes the Was span, and highlights the Now span in success green.
- Extends `ZimmProductContent` molecule to accept and forward `originalPrice` and `isPriceLoading` props to `ZimmProductPrice`, keeping the molecule's existing composition contract intact.
- Adds `selectPdpProductInfo` mapper (`pages/product-detail/productInfo.ts`) that derives `wasPrice` from `getPriceData`'s `listPrice` only when `isOnSale` is true and the list price is a real number — the Was/Now atoms branch entirely on presence of this value, so a missing or expired sale in BM correctly reverts to single-price display on next render.
- Implements variant-scoped pricing in `pages/product-detail/index.tsx` using the master product's `variants[]` as the authoritative `tieredPrices` source across three URL states: no selection (falls through to base `priceData`), colour-only (`?color=`), and colour+size (`?pid=`). A `masterProductRef` caches the master on first load so the correct `tieredPrices` are available after SFCC switches the fetched product to a standalone variant.
- Adds a deep-link fallback for shoppers arriving with `?pid=` already set on a fresh page load (no prior master fetch), using the standalone variant's own `tieredPrices` from `perPricebook: true` when `masterProductRef` is empty.
- Guards against stale Was/Now during variant re-fetches via `isPriceStale` (`requestedProductId !== product?.id`), suppressing the price entirely while `keepPreviousData` holds the previous variant's data.
- Fixes `aria-hidden` being set on the `ZimmProductPrice` live region during the loading state — removing it would prevent screen readers from registering the region before the price arrives, breaking WCAG 2.2 AA 4.1.3 announcement on settlement.

Identical to `--zimm-scale-xs` — see finding 4 | | `var(--zimm-color-text-secondary)` | `:45` (`wasPrice`) | **EXISTS** | `zimmTokens.ts:49` → `colors.text.secondary` (`colour.ts:70`) → `grey[600]` **`#666666`** | | `var(--zimm-color-status-success)` | `:48` (`nowPrice`) | **EXISTS** | `zimmTokens.ts:73` → `colors.status.success` (`colour.ts:78`) → `green[500]` **`#2d5a3d`** | | `var(--zimm-scale-s)` | `index.stories.tsx:34` | **EXISTS** | `spacing.s` → `0.75rem` (12px) — replaces a bare `gap="s"`, a correct fix | **No missing tokens.** The numeric-alias suspicion is unfounded: `--zimm-scale-200` is real (`zimmTokens.ts:157`). `overrideStyling.md`'s "only 7 numeric aliases" sentence enumerates which aliases are *hardcoded literals*, not which *exist* — the registry defines 15 (`025, 200, 300, 400, 500, 600, 700, 800, 1000, 1100, 1200, 1300, 1600, 3500, 4500`). ## Findings **1. `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductPrice/index.tsx:58-74` + `.../zimmProductPrice.css.ts:37-43` — Blocker — the loading state renders at 0px height, so the layout slot it exists to reserve is not reserved. — AGENTS.md > Performance (mobile CLS); comment contradicts shipped behaviour — CONFIRMED (browser-measured).** The placeholder spans contain only `{' '}` — one collapsible space. Blockified as flex items it is stripped, no line box is generated, and the flex `

` collapses. Measured in headless Chromium against the exact resolved CSS from my Chakra probe: ``` loading height=0 spans=[{"w":0,"h":0},{"w":0,"h":0}] settled height=18 spans=[{"w":72.77,"h":18},{"w":76.23,"h":18}] ``` `white-space: nowrap` (`css.ts:42`) does not preserve it. So `index.tsx:58`'s claim — *"opacity:0 keeps the element in the flow (height + gap retained)"* — is false on height, and the branch is functionally equivalent to rendering nothing while costing an ~18px shift when the variant price settles. This is the identical defect the same file guards against 20 lines earlier: `staticProductHeader.tsx:70-84` documents *"SFCC's `Skeleton` baseStyle sets only `borderRadius` and `opacity`, so an empty one measures 0px"* and fixes it with `minHeight="var(--zimm-font-lineheight-2xs)"`. Fix in the recipe: add `minHeight: 'var(--zimm-font-lineheight-2xs)'` to `sale.container` (that token resolves to the same 1.125rem/18px the settled row measures), or use `\u00a0` instead of `' '`. **2. `zimmProductPrice.css.ts:1-16, 31-49` — Major — unspecced brand colour decisions authored in a file CODEOWNERS deliberately routes away from the UI designer, with the prior docblock's admission that they were unspecced deleted rather than resolved. — overrideStyling.md > "Co-locating a component's theme file" / "Component-local tokens" — CONFIRMED.** The removed docblock said: *"its colours and strike-through are not specced anywhere we can read today. Adding a `sale` key that merely echoes `default` would look finished and be wrong."* Nothing has resolved that. `.docs/prd/pricing-currency-globale.md:35` (PRC-09) specifies only *"Original list price displayed alongside active sale price"* — no colour, no strike-through, no "Was"/"Now" labels; PRC-13 (`MarkdownStatus` → display behaviour) is still marked **open**. The PR body describes the choice in its own voice ("highlights the Now span in success green") and carries no Figma URL. Per overrideStyling.md a co-located `.css.ts` is *"for composing a component's own layout from already-established tokens … not for authoring new raw design values"*, and any placeholder must "say so in a comment next to it" — no `provisional`/`pending`/`placeholder`/`audit-allow` marker is present, so it registers as settled design rather than an acknowledged exception. Tier context: `CODEOWNERS:186` (`overrides/app/components/**/*.css.ts` → squads a+b only) means no designer review is auto-requested for this file. Also note the strike-through question is now silently dropped rather than recorded. **3. `zimmProductPrice.css.ts:48` — Major — `status.success` is a semantic-token misuse for a sale price. — overrideStyling.md > "The alias tier is a reference, not a second copy" — CONFIRMED.** `colors.status` (`colour.ts:76-81`) is the system/form-feedback tier — `success` sits beside `error`, `errorBackground`, `storeClosed`. Binding commerce pricing to it couples the two permanently: a designer retuning success-green retints every sale price on every surface PRC-09 lists (PLP tiles, PDP, mini-bag, cart, checkout, wishlist, recommended tiles, order history). No `text.sale` / `price.sale` alias exists today; the correct route is a new alias in `theme/foundation/colour.ts` (Tier 1, designer-gated) or an explicitly-flagged provisional constant. Separately: `#2d5a3d` green for markdown is an unusual choice for a luxury brand and is worth a designer confirming rather than a squad-only review. **4. `zimmProductPrice.css.ts:40` — Minor — `--zimm-scale-200` is the wrong alias tier for a Chakra recipe. — `theme/index.ts:47-49` — CONFIRMED.** That comment is explicit: *"The 15 numeric `--zimm-scale-NNN` aliases are duplicates of the named scale (400 = 16px = `m`) and exist only for the `.zimm-*` global classes; the named scale is the Chakra-facing surface."* `--zimm-scale-xs` is the byte-identical value (both → `spacing.xs`). No visual bug — it resolves. But repo-wide the only other numeric alias inside a Chakra recipe is `theme/components/listMenu.ts`'s `--zimm-scale-700` (28px), legitimate precisely *because* it has no named twin — reasoning spelled out at `zimmProductMeta.css.ts:18-24`. This is the first use where a named twin does exist. Every sibling small-gap recipe uses the named form (`zimmProductStyleCode.css.ts:28`, `zimmContactIconRow.css.ts:7`, `bottomBar.css.ts:112`). **5. `zimmProductPrice.css.ts:18-26` — Minor — `baseStyle` covers 1 of 3 declared parts; all four sibling multi-part recipes cover all of theirs. — house invariant asserted at `zimmTextInput.css.test.ts:81-84` — CONFIRMED.** Runtime is fine — I verified against the real resolver (`@chakra-ui/styled-system` `createResolver`, dist:1731 `isMultipart = !!config.parts`) with a direct probe on the actual recipe object: `default` → `{container: {…baseStyle}}` with `wasPrice`/`nowPrice` `undefined`; `sale` → all three parts merged correctly (container gets base + variant). No blocker, because the spans only render under `sale`/loading. But `zimmModal` (3/3), `zimmProductStyleCode` (3/3), `zimmContactIconRow` (2/2), `footerNavColumn` (4/4) all declare every part in `baseStyle`, and `zimmTextInput.css.test.ts` asserts `Object.keys(baseStyle) === parts` as an explicit invariant. Practical cost: the two spans have no baseStyle hook, so a future "make Was smaller" has nowhere to live but the variant — and `recipeParts.test.ts:15-18` names exactly this shape (`__css={undefined}`, element inherits) as one of the two silent failure modes it exists to warn about. `variants.default: {}` is harmless (lodash merge skips the `undefined` source over an existing destination — verified). **6. `zimmProductPrice/index.tsx:67` — Minor — `opacity={0}` is a state-driven style in JSX rather than the recipe. — overrideStyling.md hierarchy point 3 + "One canonical styling surface per component type" — CONFIRMED.** The loading treatment is split across two layers: structure from `sale` (recipe), visibility from a JSX prop. A `loading` variant would consolidate it — and is exactly where finding 1's missing `minHeight` belongs. Note the recipe's own docblock (`:11-15`) records that style props land *after* `__css` in `assignAfter`, so a future recipe-level `opacity` would be silently overridden by this prop. The literal `0` itself is fine (conventions.md excepts `0`/`1`/`-1`). **7. `zimmProductPrice.css.ts:33-35` — Nit — the docblock's contrast figures are accurate; one is off by 0.01. — CONFIRMED.** `text.secondary` → `#666666` → **5.74:1 on `#ffffff`** — claim exact. `text.muted` → `#969696` → **2.96:1** (comment says 2.95). Threshold choice is correct: `textStyle: 'price'` is 14px at weight 500 — normal text, not WCAG large text (≥18.66px bold or ≥24px), so 4.5:1 applies and `grey[300]` genuinely fails. `nowPrice` `#2d5a3d` → **7.95:1** (unclaimed, passes). Background really is `#ffffff` — neither `globalStyles.ts` nor base SFCC `theme/foundations/styles.js:13-15` sets a body `bg`, so Chakra's light-mode `chakra-body-bg` applies. If any surface moves to `bg-01` `#f9f8f6` the figures become 5.41:1 / 7.49:1 — still passing. WCAG 1.4.1 is satisfied independently of colour because the "Was"/"Now" labels carry the meaning. **8. `zimmProductPrice/index.tsx:22` — Nit — `variant?: 'default'` can't express the recipe's `sale` variant.** Compiles (the derived local at `:50` is a plain string) and is deliberate per the JSDoc, but Storybook/consumers can't exercise `sale.container` directly. Mostly the conventions agent's lane. **9. `zimmProductPrice.css.ts:41` — Nit — `alignItems: 'flex-start'` vs `baseline`.** Identical today (both spans share `textStyle: 'price'`). `baseline` is the more robust choice if the design ever differentiates the two figures' sizes. ## Verified clean - **`npm run audit:tokens`** — 4 unacknowledged violations repo-wide, **none in this PR's files** (all pre-existing: `header/index.tsx:238` `'240px'`, `theme/components/header.ts:73-74`, `navConstants.ts:5`). No raw hex/px/rem/em introduced. Caveat: `overrides/app/pages/` is outside the script's scope, so `staticProductHeader.tsx` is unscanned — it added none. - **`recipeGuards.test.ts` passes** (hand-traced *and* run). `textStyle` isn't in any of the guard's prop sets, so the documented exception holds mechanically; every colour/space value is a `var()`, not a bare key; `margin: 0` is a number so it's never collected. **Namespacing guard passes** — `ZimmProductPrice` has no base SFCC counterpart, so `ours`/`merged` baseStyle keys match exactly. - **`recipeParts.test.ts` passes** — all three parts the component reads (`styles.container/.wasPrice/.nowPrice`) are declared in `parts`. - **Registration exact.** `ZIMM_PRODUCT_PRICE_RECIPE = 'ZimmProductPrice'` (`index.tsx:4`) matches the `ZimmProductPrice` key in `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts`. That file is **not in the diff** — registration pre-existed. - **Tier spread: single tier (Tier 3).** `.css.ts` → `CODEOWNERS:186` (squads a+b); `ui-kits/**` → `:176` (squads a+b); `pages/product-detail/` → `:162` (squad b). No Tier 1 or Tier 2 file touched, so AGENTS.md Hard Rule #10 is satisfied — but see finding 2 for why the *absence* of a designer gate is the problem here, not a clearance. - No `.scss` added, no `!important`, no ID selectors, no `.zimm-*` global-class mirror in `globalStyles.ts`. ## Verdict Token hygiene is genuinely good: every one of the five references resolves, the contrast maths in the comment is right, the multi-part conversion actually works (probed against the real Chakra 2.7 resolver, not assumed), and both mechanical recipe guards pass. The blocking problem is behavioural, not token-related: the loading branch measures 0px, so the layout slot it was written to reserve is not reserved and the comment asserting otherwise is wrong — fix belongs in the recipe as a `minHeight`, which also resolves the split-layer `opacity` issue. The governance problem is that unspecced sale colours — including a `status.success` token repurposed for commerce pricing — landed unflagged in the one file type CODEOWNERS routes past the UI designer, after a docblock that honestly recorded them as unspecced was deleted; either mark them `provisional`/`pending` or get a designer on the PR.
